raw_response:
I farm only 8 mu, but I have been doing wheat-maize for many years, and I know this land and my labor situation. My household has only 2 people, so I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 8 mu instead of making things more complicated. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages and aim for steady yield rather than taking big risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more fertilizer into nitrogen and some phosphorus and potassium, irrigate a few times, and manage weeds and diseases with limited but timely spraying. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 8 mu because hybrid maize gives me better output and fits our local practice. For maize, I will keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate when summer moisture is not enough, spray only when needed, and use rotary tillage because it saves labor and is easier for me to manage at my age. What I want most is a stable harvest I can handle myself, not the most aggressive input plan.
